2026-12-31.title: 31 December · Seventh Day within the Octave of Christmas
readings: You have been anointed by the Holy One
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice
2026-12-31.alt: Optional memorial: St Sylvester I, pope. Liturgical colour: white. In the evening the Vigil Mass of the Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God, is celebrated.
2026-12-31.verse: From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace.
theo: On the last day of the civil year the Church reads again the Prologue of John: “In the beginning was the Word.” As one year ends and another begins, we remember the One who stands above all time, through whom “all things came into being”, and who entered time to give us “grace upon grace”. The first reading says: “Children, it is the last hour.” Christian time is not an endless circle; it moves towards Christ's return.

It is right to end the year with thanksgiving. The Church traditionally sings the Te Deum on this evening, and grants a plenary indulgence, under the usual conditions, to those who take part in its public recitation on the last day of the year (Enchiridion of Indulgences). We thank God for every grace of the past year, ask pardon for our sins, and entrust the new year to Mary, Mother of God, whose solemnity begins tonight. Pope St Sylvester I, remembered today, led the Church in the years after the persecutions ended.
outline: Ask: what are you most thankful for this year?
Christ is Lord of all time.
Whatever darkness this year held, the light was not overcome.
Count the graces; begin the new year in Christ.
“From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace.”
live: Write down five graces of this year and thank God for each.
Take part in the thanksgiving service in your parish tonight.
2026-12-31.prayer: We praise you, O God, we acknowledge you to be the Lord. For every grace of this year, thank you; for every sin, forgive us; for the year to come, guide us. From your fullness let us receive grace upon grace. Amen.
altar: At this last Mass of the year we give thanks, which is what Eucharist means. From his fullness we receive grace upon grace.

quick: The Word who was in the beginning is Lord of all time.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.
We end the year with thanksgiving: grace upon grace.
2026-12-31.action: Write down five graces of this year and thank God.
2026-12-31.question: What grace of this year am I most grateful for?

family.explain: Jesus was with God from the very beginning, before the world and before time. He became a baby to be with us.
family.intention: We thank God for all the blessings of this year.
family.ask: Ask: “What are three graces God gave our family this year?”

pm.open: Lord of time and eternity, at the end of this year we gather to thank you for grace upon grace, to ask pardon for our sins and to entrust the new year to you. Amen.
share: From his fullness we have received grace upon grace (John 1:16). What graces did I receive this year?
For what do I need to ask pardon at the end of this year?
What is my resolution for the new year?
pm.resp: Thank you, Lord, for grace upon grace.
interc: In thanksgiving for the blessings of this year.
For pardon for our sins and failures.
For those who died this year, that they may rest in peace.
For peace in the world in the new year.
For our families, that the new year may be a year of holiness.
pm.close: Lord God, all things came into being through your Word. Accept our thanks for this year, forgive our sins, and lead us into the new year with Mary, Mother of God. Amen.

illus: A family in Kochi, before watching the fireworks on New Year's Eve, sit together and each person names three graces of the year. Last year their youngest said: “Grandma got better, I passed my exam, and we are all together.”

homily: Dear friends, on the last day of the year St John writes: children, it is the last hour! Many antichrists have come (1 John 2:18). For Christians, every hour since Christ's coming is the last hour: a time of decision and of vigilance. But John reassures us: you have been anointed by the Holy One, and you know the truth (1 John 2:20).

The Gospel takes us back to the beginning: in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. All things came into being through him. In him was life, and the life was the light of all people (John 1:1–4).
At the end of a year, we remember that time itself was made through the Word. Our years begin and end in him. He is the Alpha and the Omega.

John continues: the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory. From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace (John 1:14, 16). Grace upon grace: that is a good summary of the year that is ending. Even in difficulties, God's grace did not stop.

Tonight many will celebrate with fireworks and parties. That is fine. But let us also make time to thank God, to ask pardon for the sins of this year, and to entrust the new year to him. Many parishes hold a thanksgiving Mass or adoration at midnight.

Tomorrow the Church celebrates Mary, Mother of God, and prays for peace in the world. Let us begin the new year in the arms of the Mother and the Child. Grace upon grace: thank you, Lord, for this year. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight thank Jesus for all the good things this year. Ask Him to stay with you all next year!

intro: At the end of the year: the eternal Word, the light that darkness cannot overcome, and thanksgiving for every grace.

sub: God created all things by his word.
The Word was with God and was God.
Christ is Lord of every year.
q: In the beginning when God created the heavens and the earth, the earth was a formless void and darkness covered the face of the deep, while a wind from God swept over the face of the waters. Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.

In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things came into being through him, and without him not one thing came into being.
points.apply: Offer the coming year to Christ.

sub: The glory of the Lord has risen.
Christ is the light of the world.
Whoever follows him does not walk in darkness.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
Again Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness but will have the light of life.”
points.apply: Bring one darkness of this year to Confession.

sub: Teach us to count our days.
Begin the new year with thanksgiving.
q: So teach us to count our days that we may gain a wise heart.
From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace. The law indeed was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Take part in the Te Deum tonight.

concl: We end the year with thanks and begin it with Mary.
2026-12-31.resolve: Begin the new year at Mass on the Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God.
